content: If you miss a dose of this medication, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular scheduled time. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Avoid storing it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Nevirapine is used in combination with other HIV medications to help control HIV infection. It works by reducing the amount of HIV in your body, allowing your immune system to function more effectively. This helps lower the risk of HIV-related complications, such as new infections or cancer, and improves your quality of life. However, nevirapine is not a cure for HIV infection. To reduce the risk of spreading HIV to others, continue taking all HIV medications exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Use effective barrier methods, such as latex or polyurethane condoms or dental dams, during sexual activity as directed by your doctor. Do not share personal items like needles, syringes, toothbrushes, or razors that may have come into contact with blood or other body fluids. Nevirapine should not be used to prevent HIV infection after accidental exposure, such as needle sticks or contact with blood or bodily fluids. Before starting nevirapine, read the Medication Guide provided by your pharmacist. Take this medication by mouth, with or without food, as directed by your doctor, usually once daily. Do not crush, chew, or split the tablets. If you have never taken nevirapine before, you must first take the immediate-release form for 14 days before transitioning to the extended-release form. If you have already taken the immediate-release form for more than 14 days, you may begin the extended-release tablets immediately. The dosage is based on your medical condition and response to treatment. If you stop taking this medication for more than 7 days for reasons other than the serious reactions described in the warning section, consult your doctor for instructions on how to restart treatment. It is crucial to continue taking this medication and other HIV medications exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Do not skip doses, increase your dose, or stop taking this medication without your doctor’s approval. For optimal effectiveness, take this medication at evenly spaced intervals. Common side effects may include tiredness, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Rarely, drowsiness may occur. You may notice the empty extended-release tablet shell in your stool, which is normal. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. As your immune system strengthens, it may begin to fight off infections you already had, potentially causing symptoms of those diseases to reappear. Additionally, an overactive immune system may cause symptoms to develop. These reactions can occur at any time, either shortly after starting HIV treatment or months later. Nevirapine commonly causes a rash, which is usually not serious. However, it may be difficult to distinguish between a mild rash and a rare rash that could indicate a severe reaction. Changes in body fat distribution may occur while taking this medication, such as increased fat in the upper back and stomach areas and decreased fat in the arms and legs. The cause and long-term effects of these changes are unknown. A severe allergic reaction to this drug is rare, but seek immediate medical attention if it occurs. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before taking nevirapine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. This drug may rarely cause drowsiness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can increase drowsiness. Avoid driving, using machinery, or performing tasks that require alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. Treatment can reduce the risk of passing HIV infection to your baby, and nevirapine may be part of that treatment. This medication passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and nonprescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Other medications can affect the removal of nevirapine from your body, which may impact how it works. Examples include rifamycins (such as rifampin). Nevirapine can also speed up the removal of many other medications from your body, potentially affecting their effectiveness. Do not use prednisone to prevent a rash, as it can increase the risk of a rash during the first 6 weeks of nevirapine treatment. This medication may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods, such as pills, patches, or rings, which could result in pregnancy. Discuss with your doctor or pharmacist whether you should use reliable backup birth control methods while taking this medication. In case of overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Laboratory and medical tests, such as liver function, viral load, and T-cell counts, should be performed while taking this medication. Attend all medical and lab appointments as scheduled. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed.
